sourceText: Original request (2026-08-11, translated from Chinese): 'Use our proof-or-stop method to change our command tool name from lattice to proof-or-stop, replacing all lattice wording in the documentation with the appropriate proof-or-stop form.' Follow-up scope ruling from the same user when asked whether to include load-bearing identifiers (signature salts, .lattice/ state dir, agent role IDs, npm package names): 'the rename should influence current state or future works, not past works or history, so I think it's the former' - i.e. adopt the deprecated-alias scope and do not rewrite historical records.
normalizedOutcome: A user can invoke the tool as `proof-or-stop <command>` and every forward-looking surface they encounter - active docs, help/usage text, and the session-brief header - says proof-or-stop or Proof-or-Stop, while `lattice` keeps working as a deprecated alias, historical records (the 391 story archives and CHANGELOG.md) stay byte-unchanged, and root npm test stays green.
acceptanceClaim: Running `proof-or-stop --version` and `proof-or-stop help` succeeds with no output line containing the old bin name, `lattice --version` still prints the same version, `git diff --stat` on .lattice/story and CHANGELOG.md is empty, and root `npm test` passes.
